Great — now I have a full picture of what Tutors has vs. what the broader ecosystem offers. Here's my take:

---

## Feature Inspiration for Tutors

### Where Tutors is already strong
Content variety (labs, notebooks, talks, Marp, Mermaid, podcasts, video), real-time presence via PartyKit, git-based authoring, accessibility foundations, and the i18n skeleton. These are genuine differentiators — most open-source LMS platforms don't have this breadth of content types with such a lightweight authoring model.

### The gaps that matter most

#### 1. Progress Tracking & Learning Paths
**The single biggest gap vs. every MOOC platform.** There is no concept of "completion" — no checkboxes, no progress bars, no "you're 60% through this course." Time tracking exists, but learners can't see what they've done vs. what's left.

- **Lightweight version**: Track which LOs a learner has visited, show a progress ring on the course card, highlight unvisited items in the tree view. All client-side with localStorage, no backend changes needed.
- **Full version**: Let instructors define "learning paths" (ordered sequences of LOs), track completion per-step, show a linear progress bar.
- **Why it matters**: [Personalized learning approaches boost retention by up to 30%](https://www.edisonos.com/learning-management-system/opensource-platforms). Simply knowing where you left off is table stakes.

#### 2. Formative Assessment / Quizzes
Tutors has interactive notebooks with Pyodide execution, but no quiz or assessment engine. Every major platform (Moodle, Open edX, Coursera) has this.

- **Markdown-native approach**: Define quizzes in markdown (similar to how H5P works). A fenced code block with `quiz` type could render MCQ, true/false, fill-in-the-blank — all auto-graded client-side.
- **Notebook-based assessment**: Extend the existing notebook cells with test assertions — the infrastructure for "run code and check output" is already there with Pyodide. [Automated assessment increases student motivation and reduces grading burden](https://www.mdpi.com/2071-1050/13/21/12050).
- **Why it matters**: Without formative assessment, Tutors is a content delivery platform. With it, it becomes a learning platform.

#### 3. Badges & Completion Certificates
No gamification or recognition system exists. This is standard across [Coursera, edX, and even open-source platforms](https://www.classcentral.com/report/mooc-platforms/).

- **Open Badges v3**: Issue verifiable badges using the Open Badges standard. A badge could be earned for completing a lab, finishing a course, or hitting a time threshold. The badge metadata can be a JSON-LD file served from the course itself.
- **PDF certificates**: Generate a completion certificate as a PDF (Tutors already has PDF rendering via pdfjs-dist). Template it from course metadata.
- **Why it matters**: 86% of MOOC learners pursue courses for career-related reasons. Recognition matters.

#### 4. Offline / PWA Support
Currently zero offline capability — no service worker, no manifest, no caching. The course JSON is fetched at runtime from Netlify.

- **Service worker + cache-first**: Cache the course JSON and markdown content after first load. Labs could be read offline once visited. SvelteKit has built-in service worker support.
- **Install as app**: Add a `manifest.webmanifest` so learners can "install" a course on their phone/tablet.
- **Why it matters**: [Connected learning ecosystems are a top 2026 trend](https://openelms.com/2026/01/learning-technology-trends-2026-ai-driven-future/) — learners expect to pick up where they left off, even without connectivity. Especially relevant for education in regions with unreliable internet.

#### 5. LTI Integration
Tutors has zero interoperability with institutional LMS platforms. No LTI, no SCORM, no xAPI.

- **LTI 1.3 as a tool provider**: Let instructors embed individual Tutors labs or courses inside Canvas, Moodle, or Blackboard. SvelteKit can serve the LTI launch endpoint. Grade passback would send time-spent or completion data back to the LMS gradebook.
- **Why it matters**: Institutions won't adopt a tool they can't plug into their existing stack. [Canvas holds ~50% enrollment share in North America](https://raccoongang.com/blog/best-lms-for-higher-education/) — being embeddable inside it is a multiplier.

#### 6. Additional Auth Providers
GitHub OAuth is the only option. That's fine for CS courses but a barrier for everyone else.

- **Quick wins**: `@auth/sveltekit` already supports Google, Microsoft, and generic OIDC providers — adding them is configuration, not architecture. Google alone would unlock most educational institutions.
- **Why it matters**: Not every learner has a GitHub account. Students in non-CS disciplines, K-12, and developing regions may not.

#### 7. Discussion / Annotations
No way for learners to ask questions, comment on content, or discuss with peers.

- **Lightweight approach**: Integrate [Hypothesis](https://hypothes.is/) or a similar open annotation layer — adds inline commenting to any content without building a forum from scratch.
- **Structured approach**: A simple per-LO comment thread backed by Supabase (which Tutors already uses). Not a full forum — just contextual Q&A.
- **Why it matters**: [220 million MOOC learners engage in communities to supplement learning](https://www.classcentral.com/report/mooc-platforms/). Isolation is the #1 cause of MOOC dropout.

#### 8. AI-Powered Features
[AI-powered learning generation is the #1 trend for 2026](https://openelms.com/2026/01/learning-technology-trends-2026-ai-driven-future/).

- **Course-aware AI tutor**: Tutors already has an `/llm/[courseid]` endpoint that exports course content as `llms.txt`. This is halfway to an AI tutor — feed that context to an LLM API and add a chat panel in the UI. The learner gets a tutor that knows the course material.
- **Hint system for labs**: When a learner is stuck on a lab step, offer AI-generated hints scoped to that step's content. This is what [CodeGrade](https://www.codegrade.com/) does — "nudge toward the fix, never write the solution."
- **Why it matters**: Tutors is already generating LLM-ready content. The last mile is exposing it to learners.

#### 9. Accessibility Hardening
Good foundations (dyslexia theme, skip links, reduced motion, ARIA), but not WCAG 2.1 AA compliant.

- **Missing**: Focus indicators on all interactive elements, proper `aria-live` regions for dynamic content, keyboard operability audit, color contrast audit, screen reader testing.
- **RTL support**: i18n has 5 languages but no RTL support (Arabic, Hebrew).
- **Why it matters**: [UNESCO's OER accessibility briefing](https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000380471) emphasizes that open education must mean accessible education. Institutional adoption often requires WCAG compliance.

#### 10. Cross-Course Search & Discovery
Search only works within a single course. There's no way to discover courses or search across the catalogue.

- **Catalogue search**: The community catalogue exists but has no search. Add full-text search across course titles, descriptions, and content.
- **Tagging/categories**: Let courses declare tags (e.g., "Python", "Web Dev", "Data Science") in their YAML properties and filter the catalogue by them.

---

### Prioritization Matrix

| Feature | Impact | Effort | Fits Tutors Philosophy? |
|---------|--------|--------|------------------------|
| Progress tracking | High | Small | Yes — localStorage-first |
| Markdown quizzes | High | Medium | Yes — extends markdown pipeline |
| PWA/offline | High | Small | Yes — SvelteKit native |
| Google/MS auth | High | Small | Yes — config change in @auth |
| AI tutor chat | High | Medium | Yes — llms.txt already exists |
| Open Badges | Medium | Medium | Yes — static JSON-LD |
| LTI 1.3 provider | High | Large | Yes — opens institutional adoption |
| Annotations/comments | Medium | Small | Yes if using Hypothesis |
| WCAG audit | Medium | Medium | Yes — extends existing a11y work |
| Catalogue search | Medium | Small | Yes — extends existing catalogue |

My recommendation: progress tracking and PWA support are the two highest-impact, lowest-effort items that would immediately make Tutors feel more like a learning platform and less like a content browser. Want to dig into any of these?

- **CourseVisit** (`src/lib/services/connect/types.ts`): Tracks course-level metadata only — id, title, img, lastVisit, visits count, favourite. No per-LO tracking.
- **ProfileStore interface** (`types.ts`): Implemented by both `localStorageProfile.ts` (anonymous) and `supabaseProfile.svelte.ts` (authenticated).
- **localStorage backend**: stores `CourseVisit[]` under key `courseVisits`.
- **Supabase backend**: stores same `CourseVisit[]` as jsonb in `tutors-connect-profiles` table.
- **learning_records table** (Supabase): already tracks per-LO visits with `student_id, course_id, lo_id, count, duration, type, date_last_accessed`. Populated for authenticated users only via `analyticsService.learningEvent()`.

### Course Tree
- `flattenLos(course.los)` from `@tutors/tutors-model-lib` gives all LOs recursively.
- `simpleTypes` = `["note", "archive", "web", "github", "panelnote", "paneltalk", "panelvideo", "podcast", "talk", "book", "lab", "tutorial"]` — the leaf content types.
- `course.loIndex: Map<string, Lo>` maps route → Lo for all LOs.
- Each composite LO (topic, unit) has a `.toc` array of child LOs.

### Event Flow
- `connect.svelte.ts` → `learningEvent(params)` is called on every LO navigation.
- This calls `analyticsService.learningEvent()` which records to Supabase.
- A 30-second timer updates duration via `analyticsService.updatePageCount`.

### UI Components
- **Card.svelte** (`src/lib/ui/learning-objects/layout/Card.svelte`): Has three layouts (portrait, landscape, circular). Landscape layout has an unused `metric` field on `CardDetails` that renders at bottom-right.

  export const rune = <T>(initialValue: T) => {

## Feature Inspiration for Tutors

### Where Tutors is already strong
Content variety (labs, notebooks, talks, Marp, Mermaid, podcasts, video), real-time presence via PartyKit, git-based authoring, accessibility foundations, and the i18n skeleton. These are genuine differentiators — most open-source LMS platforms don't have this breadth of content types with such a lightweight authoring model.

### The gaps that matter most

#### 1. Progress Tracking & Learning Paths
**The single biggest gap vs. every MOOC platform.** There is no concept of "completion" — no checkboxes, no progress bars, no "you're 60% through this course." Time tracking exists, but learners can't see what they've done vs. what's left.

- **Lightweight version**: Track which LOs a learner has visited, show a progress ring on the course card, highlight unvisited items in the tree view. All client-side with localStorage, no backend changes needed.
- **Full version**: Let instructors define "learning paths" (ordered sequences of LOs), track completion per-step, show a linear progress bar.
- **Why it matters**: [Personalized learning approaches boost retention by up to 30%](https://www.edisonos.com/learning-management-system/opensource-platforms). Simply knowing where you left off is table stakes.

#### 2. Formative Assessment / Quizzes
Tutors has interactive notebooks with Pyodide execution, but no quiz or assessment engine. Every major platform (Moodle, Open edX, Coursera) has this.

- **Markdown-native approach**: Define quizzes in markdown (similar to how H5P works). A fenced code block with `quiz` type could render MCQ, true/false, fill-in-the-blank — all auto-graded client-side.
- **Notebook-based assessment**: Extend the existing notebook cells with test assertions — the infrastructure for "run code and check output" is already there with Pyodide. [Automated assessment increases student motivation and reduces grading burden](https://www.mdpi.com/2071-1050/13/21/12050).
- **Why it matters**: Without formative assessment, Tutors is a content delivery platform. With it, it becomes a learning platform.

#### 3. Badges & Completion Certificates
No gamification or recognition system exists. This is standard across [Coursera, edX, and even open-source platforms](https://www.classcentral.com/report/mooc-platforms/).

- **Open Badges v3**: Issue verifiable badges using the Open Badges standard. A badge could be earned for completing a lab, finishing a course, or hitting a time threshold. The badge metadata can be a JSON-LD file served from the course itself.
- **PDF certificates**: Generate a completion certificate as a PDF (Tutors already has PDF rendering via pdfjs-dist). Template it from course metadata.
- **Why it matters**: 86% of MOOC learners pursue courses for career-related reasons. Recognition matters.

#### 4. Offline / PWA Support
Currently zero offline capability — no service worker, no manifest, no caching. The course JSON is fetched at runtime from Netlify.

- **Service worker + cache-first**: Cache the course JSON and markdown content after first load. Labs could be read offline once visited. SvelteKit has built-in service worker support.
- **Install as app**: Add a `manifest.webmanifest` so learners can "install" a course on their phone/tablet.
- **Why it matters**: [Connected learning ecosystems are a top 2026 trend](https://openelms.com/2026/01/learning-technology-trends-2026-ai-driven-future/) — learners expect to pick up where they left off, even without connectivity. Especially relevant for education in regions with unreliable internet.

#### 5. LTI Integration
Tutors has zero interoperability with institutional LMS platforms. No LTI, no SCORM, no xAPI.

- **LTI 1.3 as a tool provider**: Let instructors embed individual Tutors labs or courses inside Canvas, Moodle, or Blackboard. SvelteKit can serve the LTI launch endpoint. Grade passback would send time-spent or completion data back to the LMS gradebook.
- **Why it matters**: Institutions won't adopt a tool they can't plug into their existing stack. [Canvas holds ~50% enrollment share in North America](https://raccoongang.com/blog/best-lms-for-higher-education/) — being embeddable inside it is a multiplier.

#### 6. Additional Auth Providers
GitHub OAuth is the only option. That's fine for CS courses but a barrier for everyone else.

- **Quick wins**: `@auth/sveltekit` already supports Google, Microsoft, and generic OIDC providers — adding them is configuration, not architecture. Google alone would unlock most educational institutions.
- **Why it matters**: Not every learner has a GitHub account. Students in non-CS disciplines, K-12, and developing regions may not.

#### 7. Discussion / Annotations
No way for learners to ask questions, comment on content, or discuss with peers.

- **Lightweight approach**: Integrate [Hypothesis](https://hypothes.is/) or a similar open annotation layer — adds inline commenting to any content without building a forum from scratch.
- **Structured approach**: A simple per-LO comment thread backed by Supabase (which Tutors already uses). Not a full forum — just contextual Q&A.
- **Why it matters**: [220 million MOOC learners engage in communities to supplement learning](https://www.classcentral.com/report/mooc-platforms/). Isolation is the #1 cause of MOOC dropout.

#### 8. AI-Powered Features
[AI-powered learning generation is the #1 trend for 2026](https://openelms.com/2026/01/learning-technology-trends-2026-ai-driven-future/).

- **Course-aware AI tutor**: Tutors already has an `/llm/[courseid]` endpoint that exports course content as `llms.txt`. This is halfway to an AI tutor — feed that context to an LLM API and add a chat panel in the UI. The learner gets a tutor that knows the course material.
- **Hint system for labs**: When a learner is stuck on a lab step, offer AI-generated hints scoped to that step's content. This is what [CodeGrade](https://www.codegrade.com/) does — "nudge toward the fix, never write the solution."
- **Why it matters**: Tutors is already generating LLM-ready content. The last mile is exposing it to learners.

#### 9. Accessibility Hardening
Good foundations (dyslexia theme, skip links, reduced motion, ARIA), but not WCAG 2.1 AA compliant.

- **Missing**: Focus indicators on all interactive elements, proper `aria-live` regions for dynamic content, keyboard operability audit, color contrast audit, screen reader testing.
- **RTL support**: i18n has 5 languages but no RTL support (Arabic, Hebrew).
- **Why it matters**: [UNESCO's OER accessibility briefing](https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000380471) emphasizes that open education must mean accessible education. Institutional adoption often requires WCAG compliance.

#### 10. Cross-Course Search & Discovery
Search only works within a single course. There's no way to discover courses or search across the catalogue.

- **Catalogue search**: The community catalogue exists but has no search. Add full-text search across course titles, descriptions, and content.
- **Tagging/categories**: Let courses declare tags (e.g., "Python", "Web Dev", "Data Science") in their YAML properties and filter the catalogue by them.
